text:
sqlpipe is a command-line tool that syncs Postgres tables to Amazon S3. It reads the rows from a source table and writes them as Parquet files in an S3 bucket. sqlpipe runs as a single binary with no external dependencies.

You control each sync with a configuration file. In this file, you name the source table, the target bucket, and the sync schedule. sqlpipe supports full syncs and incremental syncs. A full sync copies the whole table. An incremental sync copies only the rows that changed after the last sync.

sqlpipe tracks the state of each sync in a small metadata file. If a sync stops before it is complete, sqlpipe starts again from the last known position. As a result, you do not get duplicate rows or partial files.
